lines.say: Fan one prompt across five agents, and let them all work in parallel.
This is Orca, an ADE for working with a fleet of parallel agents.
It runs any coding agent with your own subscription.
If an agent runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca, from Claude Code to Codex and Cursor.
Each agent gets its own isolated git worktree, so their work never collides.
When they finish, you compare the results and merge the winner.
You can drop comments on any line of an AI diff and ship them straight back to the agent.
Design Mode lets you click any element in a real Chromium window and send its HTML, CSS and a cropped screenshot into the prompt.
The phone companion tells you when an agent finishes, and you can send follow-ups from anywhere.
The repo has 88367 stars and 5656 forks, and it is free and open source under the MIT License.
Download it from onOrca.dev, or install it on a Mac with Homebrew.
Send this to someone who still runs one coding agent at a time.
